title: Exploiting Similarity Opportunities of Emerging Vision AI Models on Hybrid Bonding Architecture
problem: Vision AI accelerators do not exploit the Clustering Similarity Effect, where neighboring data points exhibit similar values, allowing redundant computations to be skipped. Current 2D/2.5D designs lack memory bandwidth and latency characteristics to support similarity detection.
motivation: Exploiting data clustering similarity can significantly improve energy and area efficiency in vision AI accelerators through computation skipping.
method: Proposes a CSE-aware architecture integrating hybrid bonding 3D DRAM to provide high-bandwidth, low-latency access for similarity detection. The architecture implements similarity detection mechanisms that identify and skip redundant computations on clustered data. Design analysis characterizes integration overhead and optimizes data flow for hybrid bonding memory hierarchy.
key_novelty: First to combine Clustering Similarity Effect exploitation with hybrid bonding 3D DRAM architecture using specialized similarity detection for vision AI accelerators.
contributions: Comprehensive analysis of hybrid bonding DRAM integration considerations and overhead for AI accelerators
CSE-aware architecture with similarity detection tailored for hybrid bonding memory
Achieves 5.69x-28.13x energy efficiency and 3.82x-10.98x area efficiency improvements over state-of-the-art 2D/2.5D accelerators
Integration methodology for similarity-aware optimization in 3D memory-coupled AI systems
limitations: Scalability across different vision model types, applicability to non-vision workloads, and overhead of similarity detection mechanisms not discussed.
primary_theme: Hybrid bonding memory with similarity detection for vision AI
